# Paper reference - all papers in one list (GENERATED, do not edit)

456 papers (404 notes). One row per paper: what it is, the link to the original, where it lives in this folder, what it contains, and why it is relevant for our problem or why not. Relevant papers come first, probably-not-relevant papers last; the code extractions are listed at the end. Goal and the nine axes: [OVERVIEW.md](OVERVIEW.md). Built by `tools/literature/catalogue.py` from the notes and `papers.csv`; change a tier, axis, verdict or statement in `papers.csv`, not here.

**Columns.** *id* = note id (or arXiv id for papers only the register knows), grep for it; *axis, T* = axis A1 - A9 and tier (T1 core, T2 relevant, T3 background, T4 not suitable); *original* = link to the paper; *here* = level-1 note, other notes on the same paper, `deep` = full-text extraction, `code` = code extraction; *content* = the idea as the note states it; *why* = novelty and relevance for us in 3 - 4 sentences, for not-relevant papers with the reason in front.

| **SN01** | GaussianCaR (our frozen camera-radar foundation) (ICRA 2026) | A1, T1 | [arXiv 2602.08784](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08784) | [SN01](papers/SN01_gaussiancar.md) [RB14](papers/RB14_gaussiancar-no-failure-evaluation-exists.md) | Every camera feature-map cell (6 cameras, EfficientViT-L2 at 1/8 resolution) and every radar point (7 accumulated sweeps of 5 radars) becomes a 3D Gaussian carrying a 128-d feature. | Camera pixels (depth distribution plus offset) and radar points (Point Transformer V3) become 3D Gaussians, splatted into a 200 x 200 BEV, fused in four stages and decoded to seven map layers. This is our frozen foundation (K61, from E27: F1@1 0.867 against 0.624 for CRN); every head reads its cached features. Caveats: features are cleaner on its own scenes (0.93) than on unseen ones (0.82), no failure evaluation exists, FP32 only, vendored rasteriser is non-commercial. Use: keep as is; optionally export alpha coverage and per-modality maps. |
| **GR09** | Sat2Graph (graph-tensor encoding: a graph as a dense multi-channel raster) (2020) | A2, T1 | [arXiv 2007.09547](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.09547) | [GR09](papers/GR09_sat2graph.md) [deep](deep/GR09_sat2graph.md) | One forward pass of a plain segmentation network predicts a tensor that encodes the graph; no agent, no recurrence. Each cell stores a vertex score and, for each of D_max = 6 angular sectors, an edge score and the offset to the neighbour vertex in that sector. | Encodes a whole road graph as a 19-channel dense raster (vertex score, plus edge score and neighbour offset for six angular sectors), decoded in one matching-free pass. Cleanest dense-to-sparse bridge between A2 and A3 and a possible fork and merge candidate source for the verified-ray builder; read, not run (K83). Blockers: undirected, world-fixed 60-degree sectors put both children of a fork in one slot, decoding is rule-based. Use: re-implement with heading-relative successor and predecessor slots, starting with an offline label audit. |
